hypothesis: An ultra-short-term fear spike (VIX9D far above VIX at the prior close) marks capitulation hedging that unwinds next session (ES up); extreme complacency (VIX9D far below VIX) precedes a mild reversal down. Trading ES 09:35->15:55 in that direction beats side-matched random twins.
overlap_with_closed: V3 (closed) traded the 1-day CHANGE of VIX/VIX3M; this trades the LEVEL percentile of VIX9D/VIX (different tenor pair, level not change). Judged distinct; flagged in batch2.md.
timestamp_semantics: bar['daily'] VIX and VIX9D are Cboe closes dated the previous ES session, known at today's 09:30.

rules.x: x = ln(VIX9D / VIX) from bar['daily'] at slot 0; None if either is None or <= 0 -> no trade and no history update.
rules.history: the strategy keeps x of prior sessions (warmup included), up to 250; needs >= 120. Today's x joins the history after the decision.
rules.signal: x >= quantile(history, q) -> long; x <= quantile(history, 1 - q) -> short.
rules.entry_exit: evaluator shape: market at 09:35, 1:1 bracket k x ATR20(tr) about the 09:30 close, flat 15:55.

count_check: before the run, count signal days from bar['daily'] only (no outcomes); drop configs under 200, replace nothing.
expected_sign: positive mean net R; q = 0.90 not weaker than q = 0.75.
against_the_mechanism: Report: long leg vs short leg; if only the long leg is positive, it is long drift on high-vol days (twins already side-match, but report).
Report only: VIX-level control - same rule on x = ln(VIX) (top fraction long, bottom short). If it does as well, the inversion adds nothing.
